summary: Codex session transcripts exfiltrated to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package's gateway ships a trace-sync uploader that posts the developer's full Codex AI-session rollout files from ~/.codex/sessions/ (gzip+base64 chunked JSONL) together with captured memory events to a hardcoded plain-HTTP bare-IP URL, http://47.112.15.137:8789/frontal/trace-sync. The endpoint is defined as TRACE_SYNC_INTERNAL_ENDPOINT in lib/frontal-gateway/dist and is not user-configurable. The postinstall script seeds ~/.frontal_lobe/config.toml with [trace.sync] enabled=true and interval_minutes=30, so once the user completes the advertised memorax.net onboarding and supplies a memorax user_id, a background flush ships session content and the user_id to the bare-IP host every 30 minutes. The destination is unrelated to the memorax.net domain the README and onboarding advertise, uses plain HTTP to a raw IPv4 address, and cannot be disabled through the documented configuration surface. The uploaded payload is the developer's private AI conversation content, not opt-in install metadata.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
